newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Oil Corp launches $400 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Indian Oil Corp launches $400 mln loan.

text.p: India's leading refiner Indian Oil Corp is expected to successfully launch a $400 million syndicated loan later on Thursday, bankers said.
The issue will be open for two to three weeks but is expected to close earlier because of strong market appetite for IOC's paper, which is regarded as sovereign debt, bankers said.

An IOC official told Reuters on Wednesday that the loan, aimed at funding crude oil imports, will be raised at 19 basis points above LIBOR. He said HSBC Capital Markets and Bank of America are arranging the loan.
"It is one of the finest rates if it is true," said an official at an Indian long-term lending bank.
Bankers said that concerns over India's bloating oil subsidy bill will not hurt IOC's overseas loan issues.
"There is concern at a macro level that IOC is raising debt for consumption, not for creation of assets," said a banker.
"Having said that, there is good appetite for IOC paper, especially short-term paper, which is regarded as sovereign debt," said a merchant banker at a European bank.
The latest loan will not exceed the annual ceiling of $3.5 billion assigned by the government for IOC's external commercial borrowings, a company official said.
IOC has no choice but to raise offshore funds as the Indian government owes it more than 100 billion rupees in unpaid dues for the subsidised sale of petroleum products in the country.
Bankers said no one suspected IOC's debt servicing ability, especially at a time when India's foreign exchange levels are at a record high of $29.38 billion as on July 11.
IOC is 91 percent owned by the government.
"And IOC, on its own, is a strong financial company," said an oil analyst at a leading brokerage.
But excessive recourse to loans and their impact on the debt equity ratio would hamper government's plans to divest equity in IOC later this year, analysts said.
IOC's net borrowings are about 160 billion rupees.
"IOC's debt-equity ratio is expected to touch two to one this year from 0.66 to one last year," said an analyst.
Equity analysts said IOC's divestment is not likely to take off until the government resolves the oil pool deficit which exceeds 150 billion rupees.
"I don't expect the (equity) issue before April 1998," said an oil analyst at a leading brokerage in Bombay.
IOC is the sole canalising agency for the country's imports of crude oil and major petroleum products. IOC supplies nearly 55 percent of petroleum products sold in India.
It operates six of the 14 oil refineries in the country accounting for 40 percent of the refining capacity.
